prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text: The ACL has been determined in accordance with GAAP. The Company is responsible for the timely and periodic determination of the amount of the ACL. Management believes that the ACL for loans and loan commitments is adequate to cover expected credit losses over the life of the loan portfolio. Although management evaluates available information to determine the adequacy of the ACL, the level of allowance is an estimate which is subject to significant judgment and short-term change. Because of uncertainties associated with local and national economic forecasts, the operating and regulatory environment, collateral values and future cash flows from the loan portfolio, it is possible that a material change could occur in the ACL. The evaluation of the adequacy of loan collateral is often based upon estimates and appraisals. Because of uncertain economic conditions, the valuations determined from such estimates and appraisals may change.

nonint.text: Non-interest expense increased $3.7 million to $49.5 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to the third quarter of 2025 due primarily to a $4.1 million increase in compensation and benefits and a $1.8 million increase in deposit related program fees, partially offset by a $1.5 million decrease in technology costs and a $1.1 million decrease in the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (“FDIC”) assessment.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text:
Interest expense decreased $5.1 million to $49.6 million for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to $54.7 million for the third quarter of 2025 due primarily to the 55 basis point decrease in the total cost of funds that reflects the decline in short-term interest rates.

Interest expense decreased $10.8 million to $149.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to $159.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, due primarily to a 55 basis point decrease in the total cost of funds reflecting the decline in short-term interest rates and the $305.7 million decrease in the average balance of borrowed funds.

tax.text: The estimated effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 29.5% as compared to 30.1% for the third quarter of 2025. The effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 29.7% compared to 30.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decline in the effective tax rate reflects the Company's initiation of an investment tax credit purchase program. In the third quarter of 2026, the Bank entered into an agreement to purchase approximately $16.0 million of federal investment tax credits generated by renewable energy projects for approximately $14.5 million. The credits are intended to offset the Bank’s 2026 federal income tax liability. No credits had transferred to the Bank as of September 30, 2026. Transfers are expected during the fourth quarter of 2026 and 2027, subject to contractual closing conditions. The Bank accounts for the credits under ASC 740, Income Taxes, and includes the anticipated purchase discount on credits expected to transfer in 2026 in its estimated annual effective tax rate.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text:
Net income was $32.4 million for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $25.3 million as compared to $7.1 million for the third quarter of 2025. This increase was due primarily to a $20.3 million increase in net interest income, and an $18.8 million decrease in the provision for credit losses, partially offset by a $4.1 million increase in compensation and benefits and a $1.8 million increase in deposit related program fees.

Net income was $83.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of $40.8 million as compared to $42.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was due primarily to a $56.1 million increase in net interest income and an $18.6 million decrease in the provision for credit losses, partially offset by an $11.6 million increase in compensation and benefits and a $5.4 million increase in deposit related program fees.

intro.text: The Company is a bank holding company headquartered in New York, New York and registered under the BHC Act. Through its wholly owned bank subsidiary, Metropolitan Commercial Bank, a New York state-chartered commercial bank, the Company provides a broad range of business, commercial and retail banking products and services to small businesses, middle-market enterprises, public entities and individuals primarily in the New York metropolitan area. The Company’s founding members, including its Chief Executive Officer, Mark DeFazio, recognized a need in the New York metropolitan area for a solutions-oriented, commercial banking franchise focused on building relationships with middle market companies and real estate entrepreneurs whose financial needs are often overlooked by larger financial institutions.

s.t: In estimating the ACL, the Company relies on models and economic forecasts developed by external parties as the primary driver of the ACL.
Deposits have traditionally been the Company’s primary source of funds for use in lending and investment activities.

Since repayment of commercial loans depends on the successful management and operation of borrowers’ businesses, repayment of such loans can be affected by adverse conditions in the local and national economy.
In estimating the allowance, the Company relies on models and economic forecasts developed by external parties as the primary driver of the allowance.

The Company relies upon operational and information systems, some of which are managed by third parties, to process, transmit and store electronic information and to manage or support a variety of our business processes, activities and products.
The Company’s ability to develop and deliver new products and services that meet the needs of its existing customers and attract new ones depends on the functionality of its technology systems.

The Company relies on its ability to generate deposits and effectively manage the repayment and maturity schedules of loans and investments to ensure that there is adequate liquidity to fund its operations.
Other primary sources of funds consist of cash flows from operations, maturities and sales of investment securities and borrowings from the FHLB of New York.

Its success will depend upon the ability of its officers and key employees to continue to implement and improve operational and other systems, to manage multiple, concurrent customer relationships, and to hire, train and manage employees.

In addition, we may rely on AI models developed by third parties, and, to that extent, would be dependent in part on the manner in which those third parties develop and train their models, including risks arising from the inclusion of any unauthorized material in the training data for their models and the effectiveness of the steps these third parties have taken to limit the risks associated with the output of their models, matters over which we may have limited visibility.

Our future dividend policy is subject to the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon various factors, including future earnings, if any, our capital requirements and general financial condition, and other factors.

The number of shares to be repurchased and the timing of repurchases, if any, will depend on several factors, including market conditions, prevailing share price, corporate and regulatory requirements, and other considerations.

Although the Company also declared a cash dividend of $0.20 per share in 2026, the declaration and payment of future dividends to holders of our common stock is at the discretion of our Board of Directors and depends on a number of factors, including:
The Company’s primary sources of funds consist of deposit inflows, loan repayments and maturities, securities cash flows and borrowings.
Repayment of CRE loans depends on the cash flow of the borrower and the net operating income of the property, the borrower’s profitability, and the value of the underlying property.
Payments on loans secured by income properties often depend on successful operation and management of the properties.

Repayment of multi-family real estate loans depends on the cash flow analysis of the property, occupancy rates, and unemployment rates, combined with the net operating income of the property, the borrower’s profitability, and the value of the underlying property.
Payments on these loans depend on successful operation and management of the properties, and repayment of such loans may be subject to adverse conditions in the real estate market and/or the economy.

In general, these loans depend on the borrower’s continuing financial stability and, therefore, are likely to be adversely affected by various factors, including job loss, divorce, illness, or personal bankruptcy.
